proposed.explanation: Article 2176 supplies negligence-based quasi-delict; Article 2180 extends responsibility to employers for employees acting within assigned tasks.
proposed.text: An architect's employee makes a negligent coordination error within assigned design work, causing damage to a third party with no contract with the architect. Why can the architect or employer still be analyzed under quasi-delict?

options.text: Because Article 2176 imposes liability for every error without requiring negligence
Because Article 1723 covers every non-collapse coordination error
Because Article 2180 can make employers responsible for employees acting within assigned tasks, together with the Article 2176 negligence rule
